question: Which of the following features MOST strongly suggests an inflammatory rather than a mechanical cause of joint pain?

answers.text: Joint pain that worsens progressively with physical activity throughout the day

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pain that worsens with use and improves with rest is characteristic of mechanical/degenerative joint disease.

answers.text: Morning stiffness lasting more than 45–60 minutes that improves with movement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Prolonged morning stiffness (>45–60 min) that loosens with activity is a hallmark of synovial inflammation, distinguishing it from the brief (<30 min) stiffness of osteoarthritis.

answers.text: Pain localised to a single large weight-bearing joint in an overweight individual

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Single large weight-bearing joint involvement in an obese patient is more consistent with osteoarthritis (mechanical). Inflammatory arthritis more typically causes polyarticular or symmetric involvement.

answers.text: Crepitus on passive joint movement with bony enlargement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Crepitus and bony hypertrophy (osteophytes, Heberden's nodes) are findings of osteoarthritis, a mechanical/degenerative process.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the inflammatory vs mechanical discrimination framework. The key features of inflammation are prolonged morning stiffness, pain that eases with use, systemic upset, and soft-tissue swelling — in contrast to mechanical pain that worsens with loading and has no systemic features.
Well done. Morning stiffness lasting >45–60 minutes is a cardinal feature of inflammatory arthritis; the stiffness of OA typically resolves within 30 minutes.
